The complete absence of contrast enhancement (`Enhancement Quality`: "None") and necrosis (`NCR Volume (mL)`: 0.0) are strong arguments against a radiologically high-grade tumor (i.e., glioblastoma). overall_comment: The patient presents with a very large, non-enhancing, infiltrative glioma with significant mass effect. The age and lack of enhancement strongly suggest an IDH-mutant glioma. The highly infiltrative pattern involving deep gray matter and ependymal surfaces is characteristic of an astrocytoma (1p/19q non-codeleted). Despite the absence of enhancement or necrosis, the massive tumor burden and extensive invasion are hallmarks of high-grade biological behavior, making a CNS WHO grade 4 diagnosis most probable, though grade 3 cannot be entirely excluded based on imaging alone.
